events.text:
🇺🇸 US loads up for possible strike against Iran - report
The USS George Washington strike group in the Arabian Sea has been loading large deliveries of standoff land-attack missiles and bunker-buster bombs designed to penetrate fortified underground targets, the Wall St. Journal reports. 
The preparations follow reports that US and Israeli militaries have drawn up plans for a shorter but more intense campaign on Iran after the November midterms, potentially targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear sites, and missile and drone arsenals.
Meanwhile, the State Department has begun [drawing down personnel at four embassies](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76702) in the region — Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar, and the UAE — citing an elevated threat environment. Non-essential staff and families were ordered out of Saudi Arabia earlier in the week.
👉 The pattern is consistent with preparation for a worst-case scenario. Embassies are thinning their footprints to reduce exposure if retaliation comes, while the military positions the munitions it would need if the attack order is given.
Iran has previously warned that any renewed US or Israeli strikes would trigger [retaliation](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76599) against American bases, warships, and Gulf infrastructure, and has reportedly drawn up [plans](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76684) to target undersea communications cables.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🇹🇼🛰 Starlink limits on Ukraine send warning to Taiwan
 
Recent US-imposed speed limits on Starlink, which severely disrupted Ukrainian [military capabilities](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76224), have raised fears within the Taiwanese government over its reliance on American defense technology.
🌏 The restrictions, which cut connectivity when terminals moved faster than 160 km/h, forced certain Ukrainian drones to slow down or lose connection, disrupting numerous [combat missions](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76535)
🌏 Interceptor drones used against Russian jet-powered Geran drones flying at 350–450 km/h became practically useless under the limit
🌏 The restrictions also affected frontline logistics and data relay
Even military-grade versions could be limited for political or commercial reasons, Taiwanese experts warn. Concerns are heightened by Musk's significant business interests in mainland China, including Tesla's Shanghai operations.
Although Taiwan's military does not currently use Starlink, the country has eased market entry rules for foreign satellite operators. The government has also vowed to develop its own indigenous version of Starlink, reducing its current dependence on undersea communications cables.
However, time may already have been irreversibly lost. China has long been developing its own Starlink analogue in the form of the state-owned [Guowang project](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75976). The project envisions around 13,000 satellites in orbit by 2035, which will not only provide communications but also carry reconnaissance equipment such as radars and optics.
👍 [Substack](https://geopoliticsprime.substack.com/) | [Chat](https://t.me/+HLrnOk92f31mYzIy) |

PM Benjamin Netanyahu has acknowledged the possibility of Israel at some point facing banking sanctions in an interview for Channel 10 ahead of the Knesset elections.
👉 He said Israel needed to be capable of circumventing such restrictions and that he was already working on a plan.
Asked about cryptocurrency and blockchain - decentralized technology that can enable payments outside traditional banking systems - Netanyahu endorsed both as potential options, adding that he had tasked advisers with preparing proposals.

🇮🇱 Israel shifts stance on Argentina’s Falklands claim amid rift with UK - report
PM Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered diplomats to back Argentina’s demand for direct talks with Britain over the [future of the disputed Falklands (Malvinas) Islands](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/62747), reports The Telegraph.
👉 The change, ordered amid the Israeli PM’s close ties with Argentine President Javier Milei, falls short of formal recognition of Argentina’s claim yet marks Israel’s first formal intervention in the dispute. 
The move also follows Britain’s recent sanctions on [illegal Israeli West Bank settlements,](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74496) announced by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband alongside accusations of ethnic cleansing. 
➡️ Those measures triggered a sharp diplomatic rupture, including the downgrading of Britain’s Jerusalem consulate and the expulsion of most of its staff.
The shift comes as Argentina intensifies [its campaign through diplomatic and legal pressure](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75426) against oil and gas exploration north of the islands.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
👁🇺🇸 Former Israeli spyware boss warns of dependence on US AI
Governments must build their own sovereign AI systems for cybersecurity rather than rely on American technology, says Shalev Hulio, [the former head of the NSO Group](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/58149), an Israeli commercial spyware manufacturer, the Financial Times reports.
AI has become a vital component of digital sovereignty, and countries should not take the risk of being cut off from foreign software, Hulio stresses, adding that other nations should abandon US AI and develop their own systems.
Although the ex-hacker boss underlines critical vulnerabilities inside cyber defense structures, it is hard to tell whether this is a friendly gesture or a play for profit.
🌏 After leaving NSO, Hulio founded Dream, a venture project aimed at providing cybersecurity tools and expertise to governments
🌏 Since its launch, Dream has raised more than $400 million and has contacts with over a dozen countries across the world
🌏 Dream is said to be trained on classified government data and built to handle narrow, mission-specific tasks such as intelligence analysis or procurement oversight
Hulio's biography makes his sudden concern for digital sovereignty difficult to take at face value. NSO's flagship product, Pegasus, became synonymous with the excesses of the commercial spyware industry after researchers documented its use by governments to infiltrate the phones of journalists, human rights activists, and political [dissidents](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/61063).
In 2021, the US blacklisted NSO Group, and Meta's WhatsApp sued the company for exploiting its messaging service to distribute malicious software. Now, the same man who once armed governments with some of the world's most invasive spyware is positioning himself as the solution to the very vulnerabilities he helped normalize.
👍 [Substack](https://geopoliticsprime.substack.com/) | [Chat](https://t.me/+HLrnOk92f31mYzIy) |

events.text:
🚨 No real opposition: Israel’s election & the Palestinian blind spot
On the eve of Israel’s Knesset election, Benjamin Netanyahu’s rivals share his core assumptions on Palestinian rights and statehood, reports +972.
They are also actively closing the only realistic path to unseating Netanyahu by refusing to cooperate with[ Arab parties such as the Joint List and Ra’am.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76417)
Polls show neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor the Zionist opposition is headed for a clear majority. 
Adding the Arab lists could potentially push the anti-Netanyahu block over the 61-seat threshold, yet[ its leaders balk. ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74575)
Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar):
♦️ Rejects a Palestinian state, supports expanding Jewish settlements, including in Area C, which covers roughly 60% of the occupied West Bank, and does not rule out [construction in the E1 zone.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73138)
♦️ Has ruled out including the United Arab List, or Ra’am, in a post-election coalition
Beyachad (Together):
🌏 Joint list by former PMs Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid rules out reliance on Arab parties, even though Bennett formed a short-lived first-of-its-kind coalition that included Ra’am in 2021 (that ousted Netanyahu)
🌏 Bennett also advocates annexing Area C
Avigdor Liberman (Yisrael Beitenu) declared in 2023 that “There are no innocents in Gaza.”
Yair Golan (the Democrats) advocated starving Gaza’s entire population until Hamas released the hostages.
The absence of any large Jewish party prepared to treat Palestinian citizens as equal partners leaves Israeli politics locked in the same narrow spectrum.
